text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Freak storms hit south east, killing one man.
- Russian woman was at the scene of a bomb explosion which nearly killed one man on Tuesday morning.
- Eleven thousand pupils will be given a medical checkup for a pilot study on public health.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Any agreement reached during military talks between the national guard and Turkish forces has to be endorsed by President Glafcos Clerides, says the government.
- Police probe armed bank robbery.
- Explosion which ripped through a Limassol apartment block critically injures one man.
- Health debate stalls as ministers fail to appear at parliamentary committee.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Sterling continues its rally against the Cyprus pound.
- Cooperative credit societies are to issue debit and credit cards and introduce new technology.
- Stock brokers call on the Cyprus Stock Exchange chief to quit.
HARAVGHI
- Deregulation of interest rates will be catastrophic for workers, says communist Akel.
- The government decides to place deposits of semi-government corporations in the National Bank of Greece and the Commercial Bank of Greece.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- New bloodshed breaks out in the underworld. One man is critically injured in Limassol bomb blast.
- Civil service union Pasydy accuses the government of misleading the public over its plans to privatise the post office.
- The Education Ministry will initiate disciplinary proceedings against its teachers who offer private tutorials.
SIMERINI
- Man critically injured in bomb explosion on Tuesday did not want police protection.
- Turkey wants a commitment it will have closer ties with the European Union if Cyprus's accession course continues.
